name: Dr. Bernadette Atanga
bio: Dr. Bernadette Atanga is a physician, author, speaker, and Organizational Health and Cultural Leadership Strategist. With more than 30 years of clinical experience caring for patients, including professionals and leaders, she saw firsthand how workplace stress and human dynamics can affect health, relationships, and performance. That experience shaped her work helping organizations diagnose and address the hidden human dynamics behind burnout, people friction, disengagement, and leadership challenges. Drawing on a physician’s diagnostic and preventive approach, she helps people understand what is driving their reactions and behaviors so they can respond with greater awareness, agency, and intentionality. She is the author of Beneath the Armor: 8 Practical Strategies for Men to Embrace Vulnerability and Lead with Authentic Strength and Grief’s Turning Point.
position: Organizational Health and Cultural Leadership Strategist

session.title: Beneath the Burnout: Diagnosing the Hidden Human Dynamics Behind High-Performing Tech Teams
session.abstract: Burnout, recurring conflict, disengagement, communication breakdowns, and turnover are often treated as separate workplace problems.
session.description: Burnout, recurring conflict, disengagement, communication breakdowns, and turnover are often treated as separate workplace problems. But what if they are symptoms of something deeper? Drawing on more than 30 years as a physician, Dr. Bernadette Atanga brings a diagnostic and preventive lens to the human side of technology. Just as a physician looks beyond symptoms to identify what is driving illness, this session invites tech leaders and professionals to look beneath workplace behaviors to uncover the hidden dynamics driving them. Emotional suppression, unprocessed stress, fear of failure, competition, interpersonal triggers, and the pressure to continually perform can quietly influence how people communicate, collaborate, handle conflict, and lead. Using a Symptoms → Diagnosis → Intervention → Outcome approach, attendees will learn to recognize early signals of people problems, examine what may be driving behavior beneath the surface, and move from automatic reactions toward greater awareness, agency, and intentional response. Because healthier tech organizations are not built by treating symptoms alone. They are built by understanding and addressing what is happening underneath.

name: Timothy Moore
bio: I’m a multi-exited tech Founder on 3 continents in 9 countries; taught at UMich-Ross with Prof. David Brophy for 5 years; am part of Executive Committee for Black Tech Saturdays, coach for New Enterprise Forum and Michigan Founders Fund; am Entrepreneur-in-Residence for CitySide Ventures/Birmingham Angels and am CEO/Founder of Clixie AI  that specializes in EdTech/Training solutions for Public Sector (Government, Health Care and Education) partnered with Cisco, Microsoft, Zoom and Instructure.

session.title: Curiosity as an Engine
session.abstract: What if the best way to teach someone was to stop giving them the answers? As AI makes information instantly accessible, knowledge is becoming abundant, but curiosity is becoming more valuable than ever.
session.description:
What if the best way to teach someone was to stop giving them the answers? As AI makes information instantly accessible, knowledge is becoming abundant, but curiosity is becoming more valuable than ever.

Join us this week with Tim Moore, CEO of Clixie AI, as he explores how AI agents, LLMs, and generative AI are reshaping education, workplace learning, and corporate training. Discover why the future of learning lies in guiding people through discovery rather than simply delivering information.

If you're interested in AI, EdTech, learning & development, knowledge management, or the future of work, this conversation is for you.

name: Devante Frisco
bio:
Devante Frisco is a cybersecurity professional from the Detroit area whose career began at Amazon, where he worked in operations before making the transition into technology. From there, he moved through IT support and technology risk before entering cybersecurity as a SOC Analyst.

Today, Devante investigates security activity across cloud, identity, endpoint, email, and network environments while continuing to build deeper expertise in AWS and cloud security. He is also passionate about mentoring aspiring cybersecurity professionals, sharing what he learns, and showing others that a career in technology can start from unexpected places.

session.title: Teach While You Grow: Making an Impact Early in Your Tech Career
session.abstract: Speaking to how professionals can make a huge impact early in their careers despite limiters like imposter syndrome.
session.description: Speaking to how professionals can make a huge impact early in their careers despite limiters like imposter syndrome. I will be sharing my own personal experiences, growth, and journey with DevOps Detroit.

name: Bryce Howitson
bio:
I have deep experience designing and building digital products, delivered across web/mobile/AR/VR/voice. 

I've helped organizations from fortune 100's to startups make their products/services: solve real problems, easier to use, and beautiful to look at. I participate in the full spectrum of launching ideas. I frequently coach innovators through best practices, but I also excel at augmenting teams in need of specific skills or deliverables. I've led teams and contributed from the trenches to help businesses solve real product and service challenges.

session.title: UX of AI: Life after the prompt
session.abstract: Prompt Engineer, so hot right now! Do you wonder why we need an entire specialization dedicated to communicating with a computer?
session.description: Prompt Engineer, so hot right now! Do you wonder why we need an entire specialization dedicated to communicating with a computer? Does it feel like "it just doesn't get you" when "chatting" with AI tools? In this session, we'll cover the history of ways humans have communicated with computers. You'll see why "natural language" doesn't seem to translate as you expected. Finally, you'll learn options for creating an interface with AI that doesn't require a special title. Along the way, you'll learn to create trust and reduce hallucinations.

name: Terranie Clarke
bio:
Terranie Clarke is a maternal health advocate, entrepreneur, author, and founder of The Heart Next Door — a maternal wellness platform reimagining support for mothers through community, storytelling, and AI-powered care.

After surviving a life-threatening childbirth complication in 2024 that nearly claimed her life, Terranie transformed her healing journey into a mission to help mothers feel less alone. Her experience navigating trauma, recovery, and postpartum isolation inspired her to write her memoir, Waking Up to Grace, and launch initiatives focused on healing-centered maternal care and birth equity.

Today, Terranie speaks on maternal health innovation, AI for social impact, women’s wellness, storytelling, and community-centered leadership. Through The Heart Next Door, she is building a “digital village” for mothers that combines compassionate human support with accessible technology designed to extend care beyond clinical settings.

Her work has been recognized through innovation fellowships, entrepreneurial programs, and community leadership initiatives across Detroit and beyond. Terranie’s talks blend vulnerability, research, vision, and practical insight — leaving audiences inspired to build more human-centered systems, businesses, and communities.

session.title: AI With Heart: Building Technology That Solves Human Problems Without Losing Humanity
session.abstract: In the race to build faster, smarter, and more automated technology, many founders are asking the same question: How do we innovate without losing our humanity?
session.description:
In the race to build faster, smarter, and more automated technology, many founders are asking the same question:

How do we innovate without losing our humanity?

After surviving a life-threatening childbirth experience, entrepreneur and founder Terranie Clarke became obsessed with one problem: why do so many people feel more digitally connected than ever — yet emotionally unsupported in real life?

That question led her to build The Heart Next Door, an AI-powered community platform designed to help mothers access emotional support, resources, and connection beyond traditional systems of care.

In this session, Terranie shares what building in maternal health taught her about the future of ethical AI, human-centered product design, and community-driven technology.

Attendees will learn:

- Why the next wave of innovation will belong to founders solving emotional and human problems, not just technical ones
- How to design AI products that build trust instead of dependency
- The competitive advantage of empathy-driven product ecosystems
- What tech founders often misunderstand about community building
- How storytelling can become one of the most powerful tools in product adoption, brand growth, and movement-building
- Why the future of tech is not less human, but more intentionally human

This talk blends startup lessons, innovation strategy, AI ethics, storytelling, and community design into a conversation that challenges audiences to rethink what meaningful technology actually looks like.

Perfect for founders, technologists, creatives, product builders, and innovators interested in building technology that creates both impact and connection.

name: Ida Delphine
bio: Software engineer and Masters student skilled in Python, Javascript/Typescript,  Kotlin, Cloud, and AI engineering. I combine technical expertise with a proven track record in open-source innovation to build resilient, scalable solutions.

session.title: Design to Production with Google Stitch
session.abstract: Stitch turns a plain-language prompt into a real UI, but the interesting part is what happens after the design exists.
session.description: Stitch turns a plain-language prompt into a real UI, but the interesting part is what happens after the design exists. This hands-on workshop runs one app concept end to end: from a blank canvas to a deployed application running on Google Cloud. We'll start in the canvas with the Idea / Theme / Content prompt formula, choosing between App and Web mode and translating between them, and picking the right design mode for the job (Thinking with 3 Pro for production candidates, Redesign for style pivots, Fast for quick wireframes). We'll iterate the way Stitch rewards: one targeted change at a time using UI/UX keywords, Edit Theme for global adjustments, and Variations with a controlled creative range when you're stuck and need five directions instead of one. Then we'll turn a screen into an interactive prototype and pull down the HTML and image assets. From there we go to code: DESIGN.md, the design-system file that agents actually read. The Stitch MCP server. It's remote, so we'll cover the real setup: API keys versus OAuth and when each is right, then wiring it into Antigravity or the Gemini CLI. Export to Google AI Studio, where we'll take the design into a working front end, iterate on it with Gemini, and break the single-file output into components as it grows. Deploy on Google Cloud. We'll ship the result and talk through what changes when the app needs a backend. Bring a laptop and set up your Google Cloud account.

name: W Scott Richardson
bio: W. Scott Richardson is an Aerospace Engineer, working for Siemens Digital Industries Software as an Information Product Architect with specialties in Computer Aided Engineering and Learning Experience Design.  Scott's early exposure to STEM programming has inspired his lifelong learning journey and passion for sharing STEM subjects and career opportunities with aspiring career professionals of all ages.  Scott is highly active with the National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) Detroit Professionals chapter and COMPASS Detroit group and ha a passion for networking and outreach.

session.title: Teams Calls To Keynotes: Communication that makes leadership listen
session.abstract: Communicating across various venues and levels isn't about dumbing down your work.
session.description:
Communicating across various venues and levels isn't about dumbing down your work. Whether you're unmuting into a noisy 15-minute Teams call, speaking up in a 1-on-1 performance review, or delivering your first high-stakes keynote, learn to tailor your output so leaders can act on it. Whether you are an individual contributor trying to secure project resources, a lead training your team, or a manager presenting up the chain, this session delivers the practical blueprint to structure your time, strip away the noise, and deliver clear, undeniable value that will be remembered.

Stop the circling back and start moving the chains.

name: Jamar Jones
bio:
Jamar Jones is a technology and customer success leader, husband, father of four, and lifelong student of human connection.

Raised in Detroit, Jamar's path into technology was anything but traditional. He barely graduated high school, grew up without a clear roadmap for success, and took on adult responsibilities at a young age while helping support his family. Along the way, he worked a variety of jobs—from mopping floors and retail work to healthcare, customer service, mortgage operations, and finance—before eventually breaking into the technology industry without a technical background or formal connections.

Today, Jamar serves as a Customer Success Manager at Truvio, where he helps organizations navigate digital transformation and business growth. Throughout his career, one lesson has remained constant: opportunities rarely come from resumes alone. They come from relationships, trust, curiosity, and a genuine commitment to helping people succeed.

Drawing from experiences that span the streets of Detroit, corporate boardrooms, customer escalations, leadership roles, and entrepreneurship, Jamar shares practical lessons on career growth, resilience, and the human side of success. His message is simple: in a world increasingly driven by technology, relationships remain the ultimate competitive advantage.

session.title: The Power of Relationships in Tech: Why Customer Success Is Really Human Success
session.abstract: Technology may be changing faster than ever, but one thing remains constant: people do business with people.
session.description:
Technology may be changing faster than ever, but one thing remains constant: people do business with people.

In this session, Jamar Jones shares his unconventional journey from growing up in Detroit and navigating adulthood without a traditional roadmap, to building a successful career across healthcare, finance, technology, and customer success. Along the way, he discovered that technical skills can open doors, but relationships are what create opportunities, build trust, and sustain long-term success.

Through personal stories, career lessons, and practical examples from the technology industry, attendees will learn how authentic relationship-building can become a competitive advantage in any field. Whether you're early in your career, transitioning industries, or leading teams, this session will challenge the idea that success is primarily about credentials, titles, or technical expertise.

Attendees will leave with actionable insights on building trust, creating meaningful professional relationships, and leveraging human connection to accelerate personal and professional growth in an increasingly digital world.

name: Greg Miller
bio: Greg Miller is a UX Engineer, Web Developer, and founder of the web agency Shrinkray Interactive. Blending a background in industrial design, adult education, and full-stack engineering, he specializes in building accessible digital interfaces, performance-driven web properties, and resilient UI systems. His work has earned multiple AAF Toledo ADDY and Mosaic awards, including honors for accessibility and site optimization. Greg serves as Technical Lead for Compass Detroit, orchestrating platform development for regional developer events like Michigan DevFest, and actively organizes community initiatives through GDG Toledo. He speaks regularly on frontend architecture, web accessibility standards, and inclusive design engineering.

session.title: The UX Cost of Security: When Authentication Breaks Accessibility
session.abstract: Security tools are designed to keep bad actors out, but modern implementations increasingly exclude users relying on assistive technology, keyboard navigation, or low cognitive load.
session.description:
Security tools are designed to keep bad actors out, but modern implementations increasingly exclude users relying on assistive technology, keyboard navigation, or low cognitive load. As frontend environments adopt stricter identity verification protocols, engineers face a growing dilemma: how do we enforce zero-trust security without destroying user experience?

This session provides a technical deep dive into the intersection of application security and web accessibility. We will analyze common UI security pitfalls—such as inaccessible CAPTCHA patterns, auto-advancing input fields, non-standard shadow DOM overrides, and aggressive session timeouts—and explore how they conflict with WCAG guidance.

Finally, we will examine modern, friction-reducing alternatives. Attendees will learn how to leverage native hardware APIs (like WebAuthn and Passkeys) to provide robust, biometric-backed authentication while automatically benefiting from OS-level accessibility features. You will leave with actionable strategies to audit your auth pipelines, align security engineering with inclusive design, and build resilient interfaces for everyone.

name: Christine Burkette
bio: I design and lead large-scale AI, technology, and sustainability transformation systems.  I help organizations turn systems, data, and artificial intelligence into measurable outcomes, without adding headcount. With more than 20 years of leadership across education, corporate, manufacturing, sustainability, and public-sector environments, I specialize in translating complex technology into clear strategy, modern workflows, and scalable systems that work. My work sits at the intersection of AI governance, digital transformation, enterprise technology strategy, and sustainability innovation, helping leaders move beyond tools toward systems that improve performance, accountability, and impact.

session.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Building Immersive AI Learning Environments for the Next Generation
session.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we teach, learn, and build, but the next frontier goes beyond putting a chatbot in front of a student.
session.description:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we teach, learn, and build, but the next frontier goes beyond putting a chatbot in front of a student.

In this session, Christine Burkette will take attendees inside the development of MYSTA × STEMCity Michigan, an initiative exploring how AI, immersive 3D environments, XR, and learning data can come together to create interactive educational experiences for K–12 students.

The session will examine the journey from concept to working learning environment: designing virtual classrooms and STEM spaces, integrating AI-supported instruction, creating interactive math and science experiences, connecting student activities and assessments, and capturing learning data that can inform personalization and future instruction.

Christine will also discuss a challenge that developers, educators, and technology leaders increasingly share: How do we move young people from simply using AI to understanding, building, and creating with it?

Attendees will see how emerging technologies can be combined to create learning environments that connect classroom concepts with real-world STEM, technology, AI, and career pathways. The session will also share lessons learned from developing an immersive platform, including technology decisions, accessibility considerations, scalability, implementation challenges, and the realities of turning an ambitious AI/XR concept into something students and educators can actually use.

Participants will leave with a practical framework for thinking beyond standalone AI tools and toward connected, immersive experiences where AI becomes part of the learning architecture, not simply an add-on.

name: Justin Beaudry
bio:
Justin Beaudry is Director of Engineering at Actual Reality Technologies and the OpenAI Ambassador for Northwest Ohio. He leads software and AI development while staying hands-on with architecture and code, combining engineering leadership with a practical understanding of what it takes to build and maintain real systems.

Justin is also the founder of Toledo Codes and co-chair of the AI Collective’s Technical Committee. Through workshops, community events, and mentorship, he helps developers sharpen their skills and creates opportunities for young people to explore technology. His approach to AI is grounded in experience: understanding where it helps, recognizing where it fails, and keeping engineering judgment at the center of the work.

session.title: From Coding Agents to Engineering Systems
session.abstract: This talk follows a software change from intent through release to examine the decisions, evidence, and coordination that make delivery dependable.
session.description:
This talk follows a software change from intent through release to examine the decisions, evidence, and coordination that make delivery dependable. Drawing on Ruslan Belkin’s workflow model and lessons from our own engineering practice, we’ll explore how to divide responsibility among people, agents, automated controls, and shared project knowledge.

We’ll also examine what it takes for a correction to improve subsequent work. Participants will leave with a practical way to identify one recurring intervention in their development process, decide where that responsibility belongs, and evaluate whether the resulting change helps.

name: Kelli Williams
bio:
Kelli Nicole is a former registered nurse, entrepreneur, workforce innovator, and AI strategist whose work sits at the intersection of technology, resilience, workforce development, and access.

After 15 years in nursing across cardiac ICU, emergency care, travel nursing, and the Michigan Department of Corrections, Kelli stepped into an entirely different world: construction. She trained through an apprenticeship program, worked in underground plumbing, and later traveled as a catastrophe project manager supporting large commercial projects after major hurricanes. Those experiences shaped the way she sees work, systems, and the people too often overlooked inside both.

She later founded her own cleaning company and began solving one of the hardest problems facing small businesses: how to create better-paying, sustainable jobs while still making the numbers work. Using AI, automation, workforce programs, and creative funding strategies, Kelli developed a U.S. Department of Labor apprenticeship program and helped structure workforce development strategies connected to more than $456,000 in grant funding.

Then life forced an unexpected reset.

After a serious car accident and traumatic brain injury, Kelli began relying heavily on AI to organize information, communicate, think through problems, and rebuild systems around her life and work. What began as a survival tool became something much bigger: a framework for using technology as a practical extension of human capacity.

Today, Kelli speaks about AI, automation, second-brain systems, workforce innovation, and what happens when emerging technology is placed in the hands of people who have historically been left out of the conversation.

Her work is rooted in Detroit and shaped by generations of family history spanning the Canary Islands, Spanish colonial Texas, and Michigan. That history reinforces the mission behind her work today: helping people use technology not simply to become more productive, but to solve real problems, create opportunity, and build something better.

Kelli’s message is simple: you do not need to be a technologist to use technology powerfully. You need a problem worth solving — and the willingness to build differently.

session.title: HumanOS: Build Systems That Multiply Your Productivity Across Life, Business & Strategy
session.abstract: AI is moving fast, but access to it does not automatically create opportunity. Knowing how to use these tools intentionally does.
session.description:
AI is moving fast, but access to it does not automatically create opportunity. Knowing how to use these tools intentionally does.

In this interactive session, Kelli Nicole shares how she began using AI as her HumanOS after a traumatic brain injury changed the way she processed information, organized ideas, and worked. What started as a personal adaptation evolved into a practical system for entrepreneurship, workforce development, automation, communication, and problem-solving.

Participants will learn how to move beyond basic prompting and begin building an AI-supported system that helps them capture knowledge, organize information, identify problems worth solving, and turn ideas into action. The session also explores how these skills can help people traditionally excluded from emerging technology build confidence, career readiness, and economic opportunity.

Attendees will leave with a simple framework they can immediately use to begin building their own HumanOS, without needing a technical background.

name: Hernando Gonzalez Malabet
bio: SHPE Detroit highlights how resilience, representation, mentorship, and community support can help Hispanic and Latino engineers build impactful careers and contribute to the future of STEM.

session.title: Leading Through Resilience: Hispanic/Latinos Engineers Shaping the Future of Steam
session.abstract: A conversation, moderated by SHPE Detroit, on resilience, identity, mentorship, and technical leadership among Hispanic and Latino engineers.
session.description:
Moderated by SHPE Detroit.

At the heart of this conversation is a shared commitment to recognizing the value of diverse technical talent, strengthening pathways into STEM, and inspiring the next generation of engineers to lead with confidence, purpose, and resilience.

Key discussion themes:

- Technical Skills & Impact: How engineering expertise, problem-solving, and continuous learning create value across STEM fields and industries
- Resilience & Career Growth: Navigating obstacles, career transitions, setbacks, and turning points while continuing to move forward
- Identity & Leadership: How cultural identity and lived experience influence innovation, teamwork, decision-making, and professional growth
- Representation & Visibility: The importance of seeing Hispanic and Latino engineers represented across technical fields, and how we widen that path
- Community, Mentorship & Support: The role of mentors, professional organizations, employee resource groups, family, and community in career achievement
- Shaping the Future of STEM: Preparing emerging talent, expanding opportunity, and using technical leadership to drive meaningful change in organizations and communities

name: Justin Coleman
bio:
Justin Coleman is an AI entrepreneur, IBM-certified data scientist, and co-founder of NeuroAIgent, where he builds tools that help organizations turn their knowledge into useful, reliable AI. His work spans applied machine learning, agentic systems, persistent AI memory, and the practical engineering required to move from a compelling demonstration to a working product.

Drawing on international professional experience, Justin brings a global perspective to AI adoption while staying closely involved in the work of building and testing systems. His speaking engagements include events with Anthropic, IBM, Nous Research, and DataRobot, covering topics such as AI hallucination loops, agent observability, and connecting AI assistants to organizational knowledge.

At NeuroAIgent, his work on Central Brain focuses on making knowledge portable across AI tools while keeping organizations in control of their information. Based in Michigan, Justin combines technical depth, entrepreneurial experience, and a direct, engaging presentation style. His sessions give developers and business leaders concrete ways to evaluate AI, recognize its failure modes, and build systems people can depend on.

session.title: AI Advanced Us Back to Basics: Building Products in the Microwave Solution Era
session.abstract: AI has dramatically compressed the distance between an idea and a working proof of concept.
session.description:
AI has dramatically compressed the distance between an idea and a working proof of concept. What once required a team, specialized expertise, and weeks or months of development can increasingly be demonstrated in hours or days.

But faster building hasn’t eliminated the fundamentals of creating successful products. It has made them more important.

We are entering what I call the “microwave solution era,” where technical execution is becoming increasingly accessible and the ability to produce a compelling demo is no longer enough to differentiate a product. When everyone can build, the advantage shifts back to two fundamentals: solving a real problem and getting that solution into the hands of the people who need it.

This isn’t unique to AI. Previous industrial revolutions followed similar patterns. New technologies made previously scarce capabilities abundant, lowered barriers to production, and shifted where value was created. AI is doing the same thing to knowledge work, software development, and product experimentation.

This session explores what that shift means for developers, founders, and product teams. Rather than focusing on another framework, model, or AI tool, we’ll examine how faster technology is pushing us back toward timeless product principles: understanding the problem before building the solution, validating with real users, recognizing what has actually become commoditized, and finding the new constraints that emerge when building itself becomes cheap.

AI didn’t eliminate product fundamentals. It advanced us far enough that we need them again.

name: Navjot Singh
bio:
Google Developer Expert for Android, Organizer at GDG-Montreal, and writes articles about Android and Kotlin.

Apart from his day-to-day job, He spends his time learning new technologies/frameworks.

session.title: Android AppFunctions: Exposing Your App to AI Agents
session.abstract: AI agents are changing the way users interact with Android apps.
session.description:
AI agents are changing the way users interact with Android apps. AppFunctions gives developers a direct, structured way to participate in this future by exposing selected app capabilities as typed, callable tools that the operating system and on-device AI agents can discover and invoke.

In this practical session, we will build an agent-ready Android feature using Kotlin and the AppFunctions Jetpack library. We will explore how AppFunctions works, compare it with intents, deep links, App Actions, and server-side MCP, and demonstrate how an AI agent can execute app functionality from a natural-language request—without relying on UI automation.

The session will also cover function descriptions, testing and debugging, backward compatibility, privacy, authorization, user consent, and security considerations. Attendees will leave with the knowledge and implementation roadmap needed to prepare their Android apps for the agentic era.

name: William Bowen

session.title: Basics of Vibe Coding Your Own Games
session.abstract: In this session, explore the end-to-end process of building game applications using AI-assisted development ("vibe coding").
session.description:
In this session, explore the end-to-end process of building game applications using AI-assisted development ("vibe coding"). Guided by experienced IT professional and educator William Bowen, attendees will learn how to turn game concepts into functional products through effective planning, strategic prompting, and rigorous testing.

The session breaks down game development into three practical phases:

- Planning & Architecture
- Prompting, Coding, & Testing
- Best Practices, Code Auditing & Refinement

Whether you are looking to build simple prototypes or complete game projects, this session provides a practical roadmap for collaborating effectively with AI models.

name: QueenTesa Fuggett
bio: QueenTesa Fuggett is a software founder and developer based in Detroit. She is CTO and co-founder of N'Charge, a fintech trading app, and the founder of EMbodied, a cycle-aware wellness app. She has about four years of experience in software engineering, and is currently a student at the Apple Developer Academy in Downtown Detroit. She builds with AI tools across app and game development and is looking forward to sharing what she's learned about building with AI agents.

session.title: Meet Sophia: A semi-autonomous Hermes Agent
session.abstract: Most people hear "AI agent" and picture a chatbot. In this talk, I'll show what an agent can do when it runs on its own: monitoring data, handling recurring tasks, and triggering builds while you're away.
session.description: Most people hear "AI agent" and picture a chatbot. In this talk, I'll show what an agent can do when it runs on its own: monitoring data, handling recurring tasks, and triggering builds while you're away. I'll walk through Sophia, an agent I built on the Hermes framework, and explain how it's set up with an orchestrator and a coding profile. You'll see live examples, the mistakes I made along the way, and the setup choices that made it reliable. You'll leave knowing what Hermes can help with, what it takes to set one up, and where to start.

name: Jayashree Ravi
bio: Hands-on person with years of consolidated knowledge and expertise in software development, data analytics/science, and big data engineering. Migrated from Fortran/Pascal/C days to jee/python/android/nodejs/javascript world. Teaching and training students in data analytics/science, data engineering (DataProc, HortonWorks, Spark, Kafka etc..), jee solutions, mobile solutions in Android, full-stack development, Lucene/Solr/Elastic search engine deployments etc...  Seek and enjoy solving technically challenging software problems.

session.title: Spring Boot Gemini Demo
session.abstract: Demonstrate hands-on using GenAI, Gemini-2.5-pro in a full-stack Java project using Spring AI and deploy to App Engine
session.description: Demonstrate hands-on using GenAI, Gemini-2.5-pro in a full-stack Java project using Spring AI and deploy to App Engine

name: Mattalynn Darden
bio: Mattalynn Darden is a cybersecurity professional, ethical hacker, entrepreneur, and founder of Mattie D UC LLC. She specializes in offensive security, web application security, vulnerability assessment, and cybersecurity education. Mattalynn delivers hands-on training that helps aspiring professionals build practical, career-ready skills.

session.title: Ethical Hacking 101: Breaking In the Right Way
session.abstract: Learn how to think like a hacker, test like a security researcher, and document findings like a professional, while understanding the legal and ethical boundaries of security research.
session.description:
You’ll learn how to think like a hacker, test like a security researcher, and document findings like a professional, while understanding the legal and ethical boundaries that separate responsible security research from unauthorized access.

Whether you’re new to cybersecurity, building your technical skills, or curious about getting started in bug bounty hunting, this session will give you a practical foundation for breaking in the right way.

name: Kiruthika
bio: I am Kiruthika Subramani, a Data Scientist at Bell, Canada. Did my Master's at MILA, the Quebec AI Institute. I have written two books on AI, delivered over 230 talks across the globe, and published more than 100 blogs. My recognitions include being a Google Developer Expert in AI, an IBM Champion for Data and AI, and a Women Techmakers Ambassador. My experience includes serving as the former Head of AI at Musitechnic Formation and interning at Amazon. I am a nine-time certified cloud practitioner (4x GCP, 5x AWS) and was honoured to be named the Women in AI Scholarship Award Winner for 2025.

session.title: Self Refining Agents That Earn Their Own Upgrades On Google Cloud
session.abstract: What would it take for an AI agent to deserve its next version, instead of just generating one itself?
session.description: What would it take for an AI agent to deserve its next version, instead of just generating one itself? That question is the whole build. As it talks to customers, it takes notes on how to get better and writes them into its own skill files, and for the deterministic tasks behind every reply, the way it classifies, clusters, and recommends, it proves itself against ground-truth labeled data. Leave a thumbs up or a thumbs down and it replays the conversation, learns from it, and drafts a sharper version of itself. But here the testing happens in a way you would not expect. Before any version ships, a friend agent steps in and plays the customer, pushing it with real questions in real time, and only when it proves better than the version it came from does a human give the final yes. This is a self refining, self looping agent running on open-source models auto-scaled on Google Cloud, earning every upgrade by proving it is genuinely better, not just a prompt we talked into looking good.

name: Rupali Sharma
bio: Rupali Sharma is a product and platform leader with over 15 years of experience shaping large-scale digital ecosystems, platform infrastructure, and trust & safety systems. Across leadership roles at Electronic Arts, Take-Two Interactive, and currently as Principal Product Lead at k-ID, she has led product strategy across titles and ecosystems including Apex Legends, FIFA, Civilization VI, XCOM 2, and Kerbal Space Program—impacting tens of millions of players globally. At k-ID, Rupali directs product and customer success for global child-safety and privacy compliance infrastructure. She also mentors aspiring leaders through Girls Who Code and ADPList, and founded the Bay Area Product Leaders community.

session.title: Strategist, Systems Builder, Customer Whisperer: The Product Leader in the AI Era
session.abstract: The product leader's job doesn't get harder because of scale; it gets harder because the job changes.
session.description:
The product leader's job doesn't get harder because of scale; it gets harder because the job changes. And now AI has quietly rewritten the job description and forgotten to tell anyone.

When anyone can generate a 20-page strategy doc or boilerplate code in five minutes, raw knowledge stops being the moat. The tool commoditized knowing; it didn't commoditize judgment.

In this talk, Rupali outlines why the modern tech and product leader must operate as three distinct archetypes simultaneously: a strategist who knows where to point autonomous tools, a systems builder who designs how organizational workflows move and decide, and a customer whisperer who spends the time AI gives back getting closer to the human users the dashboards cannot see. Drawing on real-world operating models from k-ID, where management tools are interconnected, 40% of the cross-functional team has built custom agents, and delivery cycles have collapsed, this session provides practical frameworks for tech and product teams to integrate agentic workflows effectively.

Key takeaways:

- How developers and product leaders can transition from routine task execution to high-leverage decision architecture
- Concrete frameworks for building custom agents and automating operational pipelines
- Retaining human-centered design, empathy, and platform trust in high-velocity AI environments

name: Jon Yablonski
bio: I’m Jon Yablonski, a Senior UX Designer with a passion for designing digital tools that empower people. I’ve had the opportunity to learn and grow from a variety of challenges throughout my career — from e-commerce platforms, mobile apps and internal tools to HMI systems within state-of-the-art vehicle platforms. I’m currently helping the world learn from its data at Mixpanel. Previously, I worked on the next generation of in-vehicle digital experiences at General Motors.

session.title: The Future of Software Is Personal
session.abstract: What if the next time you needed a piece of software, you built it instead of searching for it?
session.description:
What if the next time you needed a piece of software, you built it instead of searching for it? AI is dramatically lowering the barrier between identifying a problem and creating a working solution. In this hands-on session, participants will identify a small piece of friction in their everyday life or work, define the simplest possible tool that could solve it, and use AI to build a functioning prototype.

Along the way, we'll explore a new model of software creation—one where people aren't limited to the products available to them, but can increasingly create tools tailored to their own workflows, needs, and preferences.

No traditional coding experience required. Bring a laptop, curiosity, and a problem worth solving.

name: Veera Ravindra Divi
bio: Veera Ravindra Divi is a Machine Learning Engineer and distributed systems researcher based in Austin, Texas, with over 11 years of experience in software engineering, distributed systems, and enterprise technology. He builds AI-assisted engineering tools and connects production engineering with research in reliable agentic AI. He has authored or coauthored nine IEEE-published papers, reviewed 80+ IEEE conference papers, and serves on technical program committees including IEEE ICCA 2026 and IEEE GAISS 2026. He delivered an invited keynote at IEEE AIC 2026, “From Autonomy to Assurance: Governing Agentic AI for Production Enterprise Systems.” He also builds Assevra, an open-source LLM-agent reliability project. His sessions emphasize reproducible examples, engineering trade-offs, and practical techniques developers can apply to their own systems.

session.title: When AI Agents Should Stop: Testing Tool Failures Before Production
session.abstract: A fluent answer is not proof that an AI agent completed its task safely. This practical session shows developers how to test the boundary between model output and real tool execution.
session.description:
A fluent answer is not proof that an AI agent completed its task safely. This practical session shows developers how to test the boundary between model output and real tool execution. We use a small Python agent workflow to explore a tool timeout after a write, malformed returned data, and a failed handoff between steps. Then we add bounded retries, idempotency, deterministic validation, and escalation rules.

Participants will learn how to define an agent's permitted actions, construct a small failure-injection test set, read execution traces, and decide when human review is necessary. The talk connects IEEE-published research on multi-agent failure propagation with practical, framework-independent engineering techniques. It includes a trace-driven demonstration and Q&A, and is designed for intermediate developers who know APIs and basic Python. No model-training background is required.

name: Mohammad Arjamand Ali
bio: I'm a software engineer at a tax software startup, where for the past 3 years I've helped grow the company from breaking even to multi-million dollar sales. I've worked across the whole stack, including frontend, backend, infrastructure, and ML. I graduated from Eastern Michigan University in CS & Math and will be starting my Master's in CS at Georgia Tech in January.

session.title: AI in Tax Software
session.abstract: A quick overview of some of the challenges you face when implementing AI solutions for taxes.
session.description: A quick overview of some of the challenges you face when implementing AI solutions for taxes. What types of AI solutions are easy wins, where it gets tricky/difficult, and especially how the capabilities have changed over the past 2 years as AI has progressed.

name: Gbenga Olumolade
bio:
Gbenga Olumolade is the EV/Innovation Audit Analytics Manager at General Motors, where currently he is developing  AI audit methodologies focused on model risk, fairness, governance, and accountability. His work translates complex data-science and statistical concepts into practical audit procedures, governance checklists, and risk-based evaluation frameworks for large organizations.

With a background in computational sciences and mathematical modeling, Gbenga has authored peer-reviewed publications and contributed to patents and trade secrets in analytics and technology and has also presented technical and applied research at professional forums.

His work focuses on helping organizations understand how AI systems affect people, identify potential sources of systemic bias, and establish meaningful controls throughout the AI lifecycle. He is passionate about connecting technical rigor with ethical accountability so that emerging technologies are deployed responsibly and equitably.

session.title: From Code to Conscience: Operationalizing AI Auditing for Fairness and Accountability
session.abstract: AI systems increasingly influence decisions involving opportunity, access, safety, employment, finance, and mobility.
session.description:
AI systems increasingly influence decisions involving opportunity, access, safety, employment, finance, and mobility. Without effective oversight, these systems can reproduce historical inequities through biased data, proxy variables, model design, and institutional practices.

This session connects principles of algorithmic justice with practical experience developing AI audit processes within a large enterprise. Attendees will learn how to identify and prioritize high-impact AI systems, examine data and model outcomes for potential disparate impact, and evaluate documentation, explainability, human oversight, monitoring, and accountability controls.

The session will provide practical audit questions, governance checklists, and risk-based evaluation techniques that auditors, compliance professionals, data scientists, and business leaders can apply throughout the AI lifecycle. Participants will leave with a clearer framework for turning responsible AI principles into repeatable audit and governance practices.

name: Saeb Ahsan
bio: Saeb Ahsan is Portfolio Manager for AI and Automation at Henry Ford Health. Independently, he builds civic data platforms, including Access Michigan (accessmi.org), ConditionMap, and DecisionPlay, around one idea: communities deserve intelligence about the systems that affect them. His career spans federal data governance at the U.S. Department of Transportation, consulting at Accenture (Ohio Medicaid) and ZS Associates (pharma), and civic tech leadership. He co-leads AI Collective Detroit, is a Fulbright Fellow, and holds an MPP from the University of Chicago Harris School of Public Policy.

session.title: Open Data Is Not Agent-Ready (Yet)
session.abstract: Public data was built for people who read the footnotes. AI agents skip them.
session.description:
Public data was built for people who read the footnotes. AI agents skip them. In Wayne County, 60 of 627 census tracts return -666666666 as their median household income in the latest ACS 5-year release, a code meaning the estimate could not be computed. Ask an agent for the county’s lowest-income neighborhoods, and those codes rank first, with no error raised.

This talk walks through six ways public data trips up RAG, tool-calling, MCP, and text-to-SQL pipelines: codebooks, error and suppression codes, release years, geography mismatches, margins of error, and licensing. Drawing on recent benchmarks, a 2026 GSA pilot of MCP servers for federal data, and lessons from building civic data tools on Michigan and federal sources, we cover fixes that hold up in practice: typed tools, checking data before calculating, doing the math in code, and letting the agent say “no data fits.”

Attendees leave with a pipeline pattern and a 10-point checklist for any dataset they publish or depend on.

name: Adkham Zokhirov
bio: Adkham Zokhirov is a Google Developer Expert (GDE) in AI/ML and the CAIO at Mohirdev. He specializes in building practical AI solutions, agentic workflows, and multimodal architectures, with extensive experience in machine learning and cloud technologies.

session.title: Rapid AI MVP Development
session.abstract: The way we build software has fundamentally changed.
session.description: The way we build software has fundamentally changed. We are moving away from manual syntax management to a new era of "Vibe Coding"—where the focus shifts to logic verification, architectural design, and agentic workflows. In this hands-on workshop, we will explore how to turn ideas into reality faster than ever before using the power of Gemini and AI-assisted development.

name: Shugmi Shumunov
bio:
Shugmi is a collaborative technical IC & leader with 10+ years guiding cross functional teams in designing, developing, and maintaining scalable systems and automated workflows. Specializing in seamless user interfaces and robust architecture. Proven track record of architecting enterprise solutions, optimizing database queries & legacy codebases, managing stakeholder communications, and engineering excellence

When not coding, you'll find him picking things up and putting them down, shooting hoops, reading a good book, or laughing with friends

session.title: Assemble The Investigators
session.abstract: This talk covers how Lee Child's character Jack Reacher and the anime Chainsaw Man taught me about better paradigms for coding.
session.description:
This talk covers how Lee Child's character Jack Reacher and the anime Chainsaw Man taught me about better paradigms for coding.

The syntax barrier is dead. Stop typing boilerplate. Solo coding is over. You are now the Commander of an AI squad directing agents with different roles, different flaws, and different strengths. Start directing your AI crew to solve your own bottlenecks. What Jack Reacher and Chainsaw Man taught me about agentic development.

name: Boris-Wilfried Nyasse
bio:
Passionate Developer & Google Developer Expert

I enjoy my journey to ensure that the engineering trains run on time by creating an ideal environment for passionate people.

My goal is just to inspire others to continuously improve and raise their standards at all levels of the team.

session.title: Hire Your First AI Employees Without Handing Over the Keys
session.abstract: A technology company grows, and the founder ends up doing the marketing, the technology watch, the contracts and the books.
session.description:
A technology company grows, and the founder ends up doing the marketing, the technology watch, the contracts and the books. It is real work, it has to be done well, and it is not what you are best at. Hiring was out of budget then, and there was nobody to delegate to yet. So we opened a department and staffed it with virtual employees. Two work here today, one on our repositories, one on technology watch and documents. Like every employee, each has a name, a job description, a manager who reviews the work, an identity, and exactly the accesses the role requires.

The moment a virtual employee holds credentials you are not designing a workflow, you are running an identity:

- A virtual employee is not a persona, it is a perimeter.
- Hiring is provisioning credentials.
- Training is restricting, then widening.
- Promoting is granting write access.
- Firing is revoking.

You can keep calling them agents. They still need HR, and that HR is mostly IAM with better UX. You will leave with the architecture on Google Cloud and its budget, how we split work between Gemini, Claude Code and Hermes, the job description template, and the failures that showed us the edges.

name: Robert Yates
bio: Robbie has been doing QA for over 18 years. After getting a computer science degree, he found that writing code that tests other code was an interesting perspective. He's used many different tools to test many types of products and learned a lot along the way. He enjoys all kinds of technology and gaming.

session.title: How to be Detail-Oriented, as Taught by Monster Hunter
session.abstract: Want to be detail-oriented? As someone in QA, I need to be. And as someone who enjoys the Monster Hunter video games, I've found that they force you to be so in order to be successful at them.
session.description: Want to be detail-oriented? As someone in QA, I need to be. And as someone who enjoys the Monster Hunter video games, I've found that they force you to be so in order to be successful at them. In this talk, I compare the SDLC to a hunt in a Monster Hunter game. Along the way, I go through all the various areas that demand great attention to detail, describing my experiences and giving anecdotes, examples, and advice. My aim is to have this talk be generally entertaining and educational.

name: John Folberth
bio: John Folberth is an AI and Data technologist at Microsoft who helps organizations turn complex cloud, data, DevOps, and AI challenges into practical, scalable solutions. A former Microsoft Azure MVP, John has built his career around cloud architecture, Infrastructure as Code, DevOps, modern data platforms, and emerging AI technologies. He is a frequent technical speaker and writer, sharing real-world lessons with developer communities, user groups, and conferences. His work includes contributions to Microsoft technical content, technical book reviews, and articles on Azure, Terraform, CI/CD, GitHub, and AI at blog.johnfolberth.com. More recently, John has focused on applied AI, AI security, agentic systems, GitHub Copilot, Azure AI, and the Model Context Protocol. His sessions are known for making complex technologies approachable, practical, and immediately useful, with an emphasis on helping teams understand not just how new technologies work, but how to adopt them effectively and securely.

session.title: Microsoft Foundry's Four IQs
session.abstract: Microsoft’s Work IQ, Web IQ, Foundry IQ, and Fabric IQ provide complementary forms of intelligence for building grounded, context-aware agents but how do you bring them together in a deployable, production-ready solution?
session.description:
Microsoft’s Work IQ, Web IQ, Foundry IQ, and Fabric IQ provide complementary forms of intelligence for building grounded, context-aware agents but how do you bring them together in a deployable, production-ready solution?

In this implementation-focused session, we will build a practical architecture that exposes the four IQs through a shared, versioned Toolbox. We’ll explore how Work IQ supplies permission-aware organizational context, Web IQ enables current public and industry research, Foundry IQ grounds agents in curated enterprise knowledge, and Fabric IQ adds business semantics, relationships, and operational data.

The emphasis will be on what it takes to ship and operate the solution: defining tool contracts, connecting agents through MCP, managing identities and RBAC, packaging agent workloads as secure containers, and publishing immutable images and Toolbox versions. We’ll also examine an end-to-end DevOps approach using Terraform, Azure Container Registry, deployment validation, observability, and controlled agent publication to Microsoft Foundry.

Attendees will leave with a reusable architectural pattern for combining the four IQs while keeping agent reasoning, enterprise data, external research, and platform operations independently governed and deployable.

Attendee takeaways:

- Understand the distinct roles and representative uses of all four Microsoft IQs.
- Design a shared Toolbox architecture using MCP and versioned tool contracts.
- Implement secure identity, RBAC, secrets, and data-access boundaries.
- Automate infrastructure, container, Toolbox, and agent deployments.
- Apply production safeguards for validation, observability, governance, and lifecycle management

name: Pragya Keshap
bio:
Pragya Keshap is a Technical Architect and Google Developer Expert (GDE) in Google Cloud with over 17 years of experience designing and building large-scale enterprise systems. Her current work focuses on Generative AI, agentic architectures, Google Cloud, Vertex AI, Gemini, ADK, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Pragya is an active technical speaker and has presented at developer conferences and community events including Google DevFest, Google I/O Extended, Women in Tech Global Conference, CloudAustin, Kubernetes Austin, ACM Austin, and BrightTALK. Her recent talks have focused on building AI agents, multi-agent orchestration with Google ADK, and taking AI applications from chatbots to production-ready agentic systems.

She is passionate about turning emerging AI technologies into practical, production-ready solutions and sharing real-world learnings with the developer community. Pragya is also a Docker Captain and regularly speaks on Generative AI, AI agents, cloud architecture, and cloud-native technologies.

session.title: Who Evaluates the Evaluator? Building Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations with Gemini
session.abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge is quickly becoming a popular way to evaluate generative AI applications and AI agents.
session.description:
LLM-as-a-Judge is quickly becoming a popular way to evaluate generative AI applications and AI agents. Instead of relying solely on human reviewers, we can ask another LLM to assess qualities such as correctness, relevance, groundedness, and overall response quality. But this introduces an important question: Who evaluates the evaluator?

In this session, we’ll explore how to build reliable LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations using Gemini. We’ll look at what makes a good evaluation rubric, how human-labeled examples can be used to calibrate an AI judge, and how factors such as prompt design, bias, inconsistency, and model choice can influence evaluation results.

Through practical examples, we’ll compare human and LLM judgments, investigate cases where the judge gets it wrong, and explore techniques for measuring and improving judge reliability.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for designing LLM-based evaluations they can use with greater confidence when testing and improving their own generative AI and agentic applications.
